tldr: The paper proposes VERIF, a hybrid verification method combining rule-based code verification for hard constraints and LLM-based verification (QwQ-32B) for soft constraints, enabling effective reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for instruction following.
contributions: Proposed VERIF, a hybrid verification method using code for hard constraints (length, format, keyword) and large reasoning LLMs for soft constraints (style, content).
Constructed VERINSTRUCT, a high-quality instruction-following dataset of approximately 22,000 instances with verification signals.
Demonstrated that RL with VERIF achieves state-of-the-art performance among models of comparable size on instruction-following benchmarks.
Showed that RL with VERIF preserves general capabilities and generalizes well to unseen constraints.
Developed a smaller 7B generative verifier for soft constraints achieving comparable RL performance.
methods: The authors propose VERIF, a verification method that splits instruction constraints into hard constraints (verified via automatically generated Python code) and soft constraints (verified online by a large reasoning model, QwQ-32B, using chain-of-thought reasoning). The final reward is the average of hard and soft constraint scores (0 or 1 each). They construct VERINSTRUCT using constraint back-translation to augment existing instructions, auto-synthesize length/format/keyword constraints via code using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, and tag soft constraints for LLM verification. RL training is performed using the GRPO algorithm with 16 rollouts per prompt, using the VeRL framework with parallel reward computation.
results: The TULU 3 SFT + VERIF model achieves state-of-the-art performance among similarly-sized models, outperforming TULU 3 (trained with ~271k DPO pairs). On IFEval it scores 84.5%, Multi-IF 54.0%, and CFBench 72.0%. The R1-Distill-Qwen-7B + VERIF model improves GSM8K from 87.0% to 90.0% and BBH from 21.5% to 32.2%. General capabilities are preserved: MT-Bench improves from 6.3 to 7.0, and MMLU-Pro remains stable at 36.0%. Ablation shows removing code verification drops IFEval to 76.2%, and removing LLM verification drops it to 74.7%. A 7B generative verifier achieves performance comparable to QwQ-32B.
limitations: VERINSTRUCT contains only English, single-turn instruction-following data. The dataset includes only five constraint types (length, keyword, format, content, style), with improvements not observed for Startend and Language constraints (which already achieved 100% accuracy). LLMs perform poorly on keyword (0.08) and length (0.53) constraints without code verification. The approach may benefit from richer and more diverse constraint types in future datasets.
